title: M9-C42.24 — Strengthening Effectiveness Analysis
methodology: Classify each C42.23 strengthening batch using the authoritative C42.24 remeasurement. Categories: A (Proven behavioral improvement), B (Discovery improvement), C (Stability/no material change), D (Unexpected regression), E (Measurement anomaly).

batches.causal_explanation: 10 behavioral tests (property-based) killed 78 genuine Class-A mutants in cashflow_engine. This is the highest-impact strengthening batch in the campaign. The tests exercise financial invariants (conservation of money, non-negativity, identity preservation) that were previously untested.
0 new tests added. 82 survivors classified C/B (reachable contract already covered). No behavioral gap identified; existing tests already exercise the relevant contract.
9 new tests killed 16 genuine behavioral mutants in recommendation_engine. The tests validate recommendation scoring, ranking stability, and category filtering contracts.

4 boundary tests added but killed no additional mutants. Existing tests already cover the relevant boundary conditions. The new tests provide regression safety but do not improve mutation effectiveness.

9 interest-invariant tests added but killed no additional mutants. The existing credit_card test suite already exercises interest/fee calculations with sufficient granularity. The new tests provide invariant documentation but do not expose new behavioral gaps.

10 scoring tests killed 1 additional mutant. Most reconciliation survivors are equivalent or intentional. The marginal improvement suggests the new tests provide slight additional discrimination but the engine is already near its behavioral coverage ceiling.
0 new tests (conservative decision per C42.23). Loan engine is strong at 84%. 5 nondeterministic mutants preserved as reproducibility evidence. No behavioral gaps identified.

summary.overall_effectiveness: MIXED — 2 batches produced genuine behavioral improvement (cashflow, recommendation); 4 batches were already adequately tested. The 42-test strengthening program was not universally effective but achieved the highest-impact improvement in the weakest component (cashflow).
